title: Godot project asset bridge
summary: Connect desktop users to local Godot projects so they can browse resources and publish validated sprite assets without leaving Zakape.

questions.question: Should integration mutate scenes or synchronize assets automatically?
questions.answer: No. Saving into a Godot project remains an explicit artist action.
questions.decision: Limit the bridge to bounded discovery, import, folder creation, and explicit asset publishing.

questions.question: Which platforms may receive arbitrary project filesystem access?
questions.decision: Mobile and browser builds expose an unavailable state and never receive native project access.

risks: A crafted resource path could escape the selected Godot project boundary.
A partial multi-file export could leave inconsistent sprite-sheet resources.
Godot format-version differences could produce unusable generated resources.
validation: Run Rust unit tests for project discovery, path validation, PNG import, and explicit replacement.
Run studio type checking and production build.
Manually browse a project and publish a frame and animated SpriteFrames bundle.
validationEvidence: Commit 56785972bbde8c9c9ffb9e1e4da95d7c4c25ec25 introduced the bridge with automated checks.
Commit e05913c97d161376d64c238f917c50e308796c65 repaired updater state and resource browsing after review.
Rust regression tests cover Godot identity parsing, owning-project discovery, relative-path rejection, PNG import, and replacement gating.
